transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I feel like I’ve shut down and keep reacting badly ever since my work fell apart. I just can’t seem to handle anything that reminds me of getting back into business, and it's really starting to take a toll.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been going on for more than two weeks?

Yes, it's been going on for much longer than two weeks. It has been about five months now, starting right around the time my side business collapsed and my back pain got bad enough that I had to stop working.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even when you're not thinking about your business or back pain?

I have pulled back from my club and volunteer work, but it's not a separate feeling—it's entirely tied to the shame of my business collapsing and not being able to face people. I really think if I could just get my work life back on track, this whole shutdown would ease up.
When something good happens, like spending time with a friend or enjoying a hobby, does your mood improve at all, even briefly?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I haven't really paid attention to whether my mood lifts in those moments because the stress of everything else is just always in the back of my mind.
Can you recall any recent moment when something positive happened and you felt even a brief improvement in your mood, despite the ongoing stress?

I honestly can't recall any moments like that recently where I felt a real lift in my mood. Even when I try to clear my head by going down to the river or spending time in my workshop, that heavy dread and stress are always just lingering in the background.
Would you say your low mood stays the same no matter what’s happening around you, or does it ever shift at all when something positive occurs, even slightly?

I'm not really sure, to be honest, as I haven't thought about it much. I've just been feeling generally flat and overwhelmed lately, so I don't pay much attention to whether my mood shifts. It all just feels like a constant weight.

The emotional shutdown, withdrawal, and persistent distress are contextually tied to this identifiable stressor, with no evidence of an independent depressive disorder or mood-incongruent symptoms.
